result.stdout:
Usage: reqjet run <path>... [options]

Sends the requests in .http files the same way the Reqjet app does: environments, @variables,
scripts, assertions and chaining all work. A path can be:
  a folder         every request in its .http files (and below), in tree order
  a workspace      each of its folders in turn, as above (a .reqjet-workspace file saved by the app);
                   a folder it names that isn't there is an error
  a .http file     every request in the file
  a runbook (.md)  its steps in order, stopping at the first that doesn't finish
  a script (.js)   the script, sending requests by # @name
Runbooks and scripts only run when named: running a folder or workspace sends its .http requests and nothing else.

Options:
  -e, --env <name>        environment from http-client.env.json (and .user)
  --var <name=value>      a value for {{name}}, over everything else (repeatable); also answers
                          runbook inputs and script input()
  --yes                   answer yes to confirmations (otherwise asked, or declined when not interactive)
  --junit <file>          also write the results as JUnit XML (for CI test reports)
  --summary <file>        also append the results as Markdown: --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" puts a
                          table on the GitHub Actions run page
  --data <file>           run each .http file once per row of a CSV or JSON file, with the row's
                          values as {{variables}} (a file's own # @reqjet.data is used otherwise)
  --update-snapshots      save responses as the new snapshots (# @reqjet.snapshot) instead of comparing;
                          without it a missing snapshot fails
  --root <folder>         where to stop looking for env files (default: the git repository)
  --proxy <url>           send through this proxy (http://user:pass@host:port), or "none"; default: the
                          system proxy (HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY, else the OS settings)
  --proxy-bypass <hosts>  hosts that skip --proxy: "*.corp.
[truncated]

result.stdout:
Usage: reqjet load <file.http> [--name <request>] [options]

A quick load test of one request: sends it once normally (getting OAuth tokens and running its scripts), then over
and over, several at once, and reports requests per second, response time percentiles and failures.
A send fails on no response, a 4xx/5xx status, or a failed # @reqjet.assert.

Options (and -e, --var, --root and --proxy, as for reqjet run):
  --name <request>        the request's # @name or title (not needed when the file has one request)
  -n, --requests <count>  how many to send (default 100)
  -c, --concurrency <n>   how many at once (default 10)
  --duration <time>       keep sending for this long instead, e.g. 30s or 2m
  --max-p95 <ms>          fail when 95% of requests aren't faster than this, e.g. 500 or 500ms
  --max-error-rate <%>    fail when more than this percentage of requests fail, e.g. 1
  --k6 <file>             don't run it: write the same test (settings and thresholds) as a k6 script,
                          or - to print it

It's a quick check of one endpoint, the same as the app's Quick load test. For multi-step scenarios,
ramp-up or load from several machines, use a load-testing tool such as k6.

Exit code: 0 when the thresholds were met (or none were given and nothing failed), 1 otherwise.
Only load test a site you own or have permission to test.

result.stdout:
Usage: reqjet mock <path>... [--port 4010] [-e <env>]

Serves canned responses on http://localhost:<port> (this machine only) until Ctrl+C, for building a front end
or testing a client without the real API. A path can be:
  a folder or .http file   each request's method and path, answered with its saved snapshot
                           (# @reqjet.snapshot); a {{variable}} in the path matches any value, and
                           OpenAPI descriptions the files name (# @reqjet.openapi) are mocked too
  a workspace              each of its folders, as above (a .reqjet-workspace file saved by the app)
  an OpenAPI description   each operation, answered with its example (or one made from the schema)
-e picks the environment used to read base paths ({{baseUrl}} = https://host/api mocks /api/...).
